claims.text: Adding approximately 1–5 at.% Ag to CoCrFeNi will enable in-situ formation of Ag-rich phases during sliding.
The Ag-rich phases will reduce the coefficient of friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The Ag-rich phases will reduce wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C.
Ag addition will produce segregated, silver-enriched films or oxides at the sliding interface.
During sliding and thermal exposure, Ag will preferentially segregate to the wear surface.
Surface-segregated Ag will form a thin and stable lubricious film.
The proposed Ag-rich film will have low shear strength.
The Ag-rich film will act as a self-lubricating layer that reduces friction.
The Ag-rich film will act as a self-lubricating layer that reduces wear.
The self-lubricating film will remain effective across the extended room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi tested under the same conditions, Ag-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction throughout the full temperature range.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi tested under the same conditions, Ag-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate throughout the full temperature range.
Continuous formation of a lubricious Ag-rich phase is the cause of the predicted friction and wear improvements.
The proposed operating boundaries are ambient air, an approximately 10 N constant load, and temperatures from room temperature to 800 °C.
The optimum Ag content and Ag distribution dynamics may depend on load and temperature history.
